title: How startups grow
examples: What is the difference between a good idea and a viable business?
How do I know if my product is actually useful to people?
When should I ask for investment money?

explain.say: First you need a solid business idea to start with.
Next you turn that idea into a basic working product.
You must test that product with real potential customers.
Once you prove people want it you need money to grow bigger.
Remember that failure is a normal and common part of this journey.

items: It is feedback, not a final stop.
Adapt your plan based on what failed.

explain.say: Imagine you want to start a local tutoring service.

faq.q: What exactly is a minimum viable product?
faq.a: It is the simplest version of your product that lets you test your core idea. You can ask if it is the same as a prototype or a basic model.
asks: How small should my first product be?
Do I need to build the whole thing first?

faq.q: How do I know if my idea is good enough?
faq.a: You must check if people are willing to pay money for the solution. You can also ask if I need to survey people first.
asks: Is having a good idea enough?
How do I test my market?
Should I talk to potential users?

faq.q: What is the difference between funding sources?
faq.a: Bootstrapping means using your own money, while external funding comes from investors. You might also ask about grants or loans.
asks: Is venture capital the only option?

faq.q: If my first product fails, what should I do?
faq.a: You should treat it as valuable data showing what does not work. Then you use that knowledge to adjust your next attempt.
asks: Can I restart after a failure?
How do I pivot my business?

faq.q: Do I need a perfect business plan before starting?
faq.a: No, a detailed plan can slow you down. It is better to start small and build the plan as you learn. You can ask if I need to write a book first.
asks: Should I write a business plan?
Is a plan more important than action?

facts: A Minimum Viable Product is the most basic version of a product.
Bootstrapping means funding a business using personal savings or early revenue.
Customer feedback is essential for improving a product's viability.
Failure in entrepreneurship is viewed as a learning opportunity.

quiz.say: A baker wants to test if people like sourdough bread. Which stage should they focus on first?
quiz.why: Testing with customers tells you if the market actually wants the product.

wrong.1: Thinking about the idea is only the very first step.
wrong.2: Building a full product before testing wastes time and money.
wrong.3: You should not ask for money until you prove people will buy it.

quiz.say: A student builds a simple website mockup to test if people want an online study guide. This mockup represents which stage?
quiz.why: An MVP is a basic, functional version to gather real user data.

wrong.0: Funding happens after you prove the concept works.
wrong.2: A prototype is usually a non-functional model for design testing.
wrong.3: The final product is what you build after successful testing.

quiz.say: If a startup uses only its own profits to grow, this method is called:
quiz.why: Bootstrapping means funding growth from internal, self-generated cash flow.

wrong.0: Seed funding is a specific, early round of external money.
wrong.2: Venture Capital comes from large external investment firms.
wrong.3: Angel Investment comes from wealthy individuals, not just self-funding.
